parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shivasharanappa, Ramesh, Chandra Kant, Suresh, Shivakumar Manase, Gurlingappa Dhotre, Khashinath, Mallinath, Basawantraya, Hanumanthraya, Panditrao, Anneppa, Sharannamma
parties.respondent_defendant: Sangameshwar, Nilabai, Suvarna, Sugalabai, Shantabai, Kashinath, Mallinath, Basawantraya, Hanumanthraya, Panditrao, Anneppa, Shankar, Gurubai

facts_of_case: The parties are agriculturalists from various villages. The case is about partition of properties.

legal_principles.principle: A person who is not a member of the coparcenary cannot claim a share in the joint family properties.
legal_principles.held: Chandanna himself having died prior to the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, and no partition having taken place during his lifetime, on his death, no right accrued in favour of the second plaintiff; that she was not possessed of any properties of the family in her capacity as widow of a member of coparcenary.
use_in: partition cases involving Hindu joint families

legal_principles.principle: A person who is not a member of the coparcenary cannot claim a share in the joint family properties, even if they are related to the members of the coparcenary.
legal_principles.held: that these defendants being granddaughters of propositor Shivalingappa being grandsons of Shivalingappa's daughter Kallawwa and 17th defendant Gurubai being granddaughter of propositor through his son Chandanna, whom Neelabai married, and therefore while the plaintiffs may be given their share as per law, these defendants also should be given their legitimate share in accordance with law from out of the joint family properties.
use_in: partition cases involving Hindu joint families and related family members

outcome.final_order: The appeal is dismissed as the trial court's decision is upheld.
